schema_description: The openEHR ADL 1.4 operational template as openehr-sdk-go generates it: the pinned openehr_am_1.4.0 schema over the RM root, with the classes of the AM Release-1.4 template schema and each AOM 1.4 class in the form the AM Release-1.4 schemas give it.

classes_left_out.reason: the AM Release-1.4 schema names the class C_CODE_PHRASE, which the root declares in the schema's form.
the AM Release-1.4 schema names the class C_DV_ORDINAL, which the root declares in the schema's form.
the AM Release-1.4 schema names the class C_DV_QUANTITY, which the root declares in the schema's form.

type_aliases.reason: older template tools write an archetype root of an operational template as xsi:type T_ARCHETYPE_ROOT, a name no schema declares; it reads as the C_ARCHETYPE_ROOT the template schema declares.

dropped_elements.reason: a legacy element Archetype Designer writes on every attribute constraint, which no AOM class declares and the schema accepts fixed to false, at two positions; false is written false or 0, as the schema's boolean allows.

anonymous_type_names.reason: the schema declares the type of the constraints element anonymously.
the schema declares the type of the items element anonymously.

schema_forms.reason: the schema type ORDINAL_SYMBOL is a choice between the elements of a DV_CODED_TEXT and those of a CODE_PHRASE, which P_BMM cannot express.
the schema types the symbol of a SCALE as ORDINAL_SYMBOL, the choice ORDINAL.symbol takes.

C_DURATION.name: C_DURATION
C_DURATION.documentation:
ISO 8601-compatible constraint on instances of Duration. In ISO 8601 terms, constraints might are of the form “PWD” (weeks and/or days), “PDTHMS” (days, hours, minutes, seconds) and so on.

Both range and the constraint pattern can be set at the same time, corresponding to the ADL constraint `"PWD/|P0W..P50W|"`.

As for all of openEHR, two ISO 8601 exceptions are allowed: 

* the ‘W’ (week) designator can be mixed in - the allowed patterns are: `P[Y|y][M|m][D|d][T[H|h][M|m][S|s]]` and `P[W|w]`;
* the values used in an interval constraint may be negated, i.e. a leading minus (`'-'`) sign may be used.

Reason: the AM Release-1.4 schema constrains a duration by a pattern, where the BMM gives a flag for each of its designators. Upstream: resources/its-xml/components/AM/Release-1.4/Archetype.xsd:353.
